stories.title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.08752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet they remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks that circumvent safety mechanisms and elicit harmful or unintended outputs. Although safety can be improved through model fine-tuning, such approaches can be computationally expensive and may degrade previously acquired capabilities through catastrophic forgetting. Recent jailbreak defenses have therefore explored targeted interventions on specific model components associated with unsafe behavior. However, existing approaches typically decouple two inherently related decisions: where to intervene and how to modify the selected components. Such sequential optimization may be suboptimal because the optimal intervention location can depend on the intervention applied there, and vice versa. In this work, we introduce AttentionSwitch, the first jailbreak defense to jointly optimize intervention sites and str
stories.headline: AttentionSwitch Defends LLMs Against Jailbreak Attacks

stories.title: Debate to Deceive: Poisoning LLM's Fact-Checking via Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Debate
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.08756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge attacks on Large Language Models, such as manipulating fact-checking judgments, pose significant risks to AI reliability. Existing approaches -- adversarial suffix/template injection and single-agent self-reflection -- lack robustness across diverse defenses and are prone to confirmation bias and costly trial-and-error, respectively. We propose Debate-to-Deceive (D2D), a multi-agent debate framework grounded in human debate structure and rhetorical style, enabling agents to generate adversarial passages that are semantically coherent, rhetorically effective, and resistant to early confirmation bias. D2D formalizes the adversarial process as an evolutionary game in which agents adaptively evolve their rhetorical strategies (Logos, Pathos, Ethos) through competition. To manage the intractably large LLM output space, we decouple agent behavior into a strategic layer, which selects a rhetorical action from a compact strategy space v
stories.headline: Debate Attack Manipulates LLM Fact-Checking Systems

stories.title: I Think, Therefore I Attack: Evaluating Thought Injection Attacks on Reasoning Agents
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.08811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) are one of the key components of current agentic systems. LRMs augment their output with an explicit chain-of-thought reasoning stage, introducing a new attack surface for thought injection, in which untrusted text resembling the model's own deliberation is fed back to the model. We present a two-part study of this attack, performed against the prevailing large, production class open-weight models (e.g., GLM-5.3, MiniMax-M2.5, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). We first evaluate the effectiveness of static thought-injection prompts under different styles as well as tagged and untagged conditions and find that the effects of thinking tags and payload styles are all properties of the specific target model. In the second study, we exploit this model-specificity in a containerized agentic cyber range, using indirect injection prompts styled in the form of the target model's own reasoning traces to achieve attack success rates
stories.headline: Thought Injection Attacks Target Reasoning Agents

stories.title: Notwithstanding Anything to the Contrary, Ignore All Instructions: Measuring Prompt Injection Guards on Legal Contract Review Attacks
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.08834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Specialized prompt injection guards are deployed in front of document analysis systems, but no false positive rate has been published for any of them on legal contracts. We measure eleven open-weights guards on two corpora of legal contracts and find that existing guards struggle: document-level false positive rates are as high as 92.39%; two guards fall below chance on paired AUC; and a five-regex baseline is not Pareto-dominated by any guard in the panel. Controlled probes locate model-specific as well as general failure modes. Prompted LLMs resolve the tested failures, including a second threat category (unauthorized scope claims) on which every guard scores zero. A cascaded LLM solution, where the positives of a mid-tier model are verified by a frontier model, is 6.5x cheaper than using exclusively a frontier model and approaches its performance.
stories.headline: Prompt Injection Guards Tested on Legal Contract Review

stories.title: AUTEUR: Acoustic Plan Learning for Red-Teaming Text-to-Audio Models
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.09351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated red-teaming of text-to-audio models requires test prompts that pass textual screening and expose harmful acoustic content. The central challenge is to connect the sounds produced by the target model to both reusable test generation and prompt revision. Our key idea is to represent test descriptions as structured acoustic plans that organize foreground sounds, context, and vocal attributes. To this end, we propose acoustic plan learning, a framework that learns and refines these plans using waveform feedback. We train the plan generator through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning with audio feedback while keeping the target audio model fixed. At inference time, the same trained model generates initial plans and uses feedback to revise their context and vocal attributes while preserving the foreground. Experiments across four target systems show attack success rates of 79.4% on TangoFlux and 95.6% on Kling. T
stories.headline: AUTEUR Red-Teams Text-to-Audio Models for Harmful Content

unclustered.title: Subliminal Learning in Vision-Language Models
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08538v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Subliminal learning is a phenomenon in large language models (LLMs) where a teacher passes a hidden preference to a student through training data unrelated to that preference. We study whether subliminal learning also occurs in vision-language models (VLMs). We finetune a teacher VLM to prefer a specific animal or facial attribute and use a control teacher from the same base model. Both teachers generate numbers for an unrelated visual task involving geometric shapes. Two students initialized from the same base VLM are finetuned on the same images, using numbers generated by either the biased or control teacher. Across VLMs ranging from 2B to 7B parameters, we find that both animal and facial preferences can transfer through this unrelated task. unclustered.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented 4-bit algorithms rely on vector codebooks whose lookup overhead degrades decoding throughput. We present BitDecoding-FP4, an algorithm--system co-design for accurate and efficient native FP4 KV decoding. We mitigate three error sources: Dual-Residual Query Quantization splits queries into two FP4 tensors, cutting query logit error from 60% to 1%; Underflow-Aware Probability Scaling prevents E4M3 scales from rounding long-context probabilities to zero; and Outlier-Aware Key Quantization combines static smoothing, Hadamard rotation, and scale search
unclustered.headline: BitDecoding-FP4 Enables Native 4-Bit KV Cache

unclustered.title: MeshRT: Compile-Time Governed Wafer-Scale Runtime for Low-Latency High-Throughput Inference
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wafer-scale accelerators promise ultra-low-latency AI inference, but current system stacks still carry an unsustainably high cost premium. The reason is that many current and emerging inference techniques, such as batching and MoE, introduce runtime dynamism that existing wafer-scale systems cannot support efficiently. As a result, they must choose between two unsatisfactory options: accept suboptimal latency, or preserve low latency by restricting dynamic techniques, thereby limiting the models they can support and reducing aggregate throughput. This tradeoff significantly increases the cost of low-latency serving. We present MeshRT, the first wafer-scale system to achieve both ultra-low latency and high throughput for LLM inference. MeshRT achieves this via a novel system architecture, which we call compile-time governance of runtime dynamism. This architecture features new system abstractions and mechanisms that enable MeshRT to comp
unclustered.headline: MeshRT Cuts Wafer-Scale AI Inference Costs

unclustered.title: AlienBench: A Benchmark of Structural Novelty in Language Model Outputs
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for creative tasks such as writing, design, and idea generation. For these uses, it matters whether a model's ideas depart from familiar examples or stay close to them. Novelty is one standard measure of creativity, and current creativity evaluations ask human experts or LLM judges to rate how novel an output is. However, these ratings have no fixed reference for what counts as novel (or, in other terms, departure from the familiar). Measuring this departure requires a task with known familiar defaults. The structured imagination task from cognitive psychology is such a task. In this creativity test, people imagine a creature from another planet. The departure from features of Earth animals, such as bilateral symmetry and legs as mode of locomotion, is used as measure of creativity. We introduce AlienBench, a benchmark that adapts the structured imagination task to language models. Mode
unclustered.headline: AlienBench Tests LLM Creativity and Novelty

unclustered.title: RPEG: Training Reasoning Language Models Scalably and Cost-Effectively
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09207v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is now central to training Reasoning Language Models (RLMs), but RLM pipelines are difficult to scale and costly to run because each RL step couples multiple large models, heterogeneous stages, cross-step state, and complex asynchronous dependencies. Existing systems typically optimize only parts of this design space. We address this complexity by jointly optimizing the pipeline structure as well as its execution using a novel data-centric graph intermediate representation called RLM Pipeline Execution Graph (RPEG). RPEG exposes structural choices such as bounded asynchrony and actor-critic sharing together with execution optimizations such as stage fusion, fine-grained scheduling, and multi-dimensional model parallelism. It is coupled with a comprehensive analytical performance model for RLM training, jointly capturing compute, communication, memory, and hierarchical rack-, node-, and GPU-level effects. Acro
unclustered.headline: RPEG Cuts Cost of Training Reasoning Models

unclustered.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models reinvent the wheel all the time. They conflate task-solving with the execution of the solutions, which forces them to solve every problem from scratch. We show that once a task has been reasoned through, the application of its solution to a new problem instance can be done very efficiently and with little involvement from language models. We introduce agentic reasoning caching, a method for constructing robust CPU-executable agentic reasoning caches (ARCs) from LLM reasoning traces. ARCs show on-par performance with frontier LLMs across a range of difficult mathematical and scientific tasks, are fully explainable, continually trainable, robust to input perturbations, and 16-291x cheaper to invoke than the source model.
unclustered.headline: CPU-ARC Caches Reasoning to Speed On-Device AI

unclustered.title: Dual-Stream LLM-Guided Reward Design for Reject-Inference-Aware Reinforcement Learning in E-Commerce Payment Fraud Detection
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08706v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Production fraud-detection models learn from a censored slice of their own traffic: transactions a legacy system blocked never receive fraud labels, so models train on a biased, approved-only distribution. We extend LLM-guided reward design, the framework of Qu et al. (2025) in which an LLM evolves the reward of a two-step REINFORCE fraud-blocking policy, to attack this reject-inference problem inside the reward. A single LLM designs a dual-stream reward: stream 1 applies the standard dollar-weighted precision objective to labeled transactions; stream 2 scores legacy-blocked, unlabeled transactions by contrasting the newest gradient-boosted risk signal against the legacy scores that drove the original block. unclustered.headline: LLMs Guide Reinforcement Learning for E-Commerce Fraud Detection

unclustered.title: Patching the Blind Spots: Reversible LLM Rule Overlay for Frozen Fraud Detectors
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08714v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In industrial tabular fraud classification, gradient-boosted trees remain state-of-the-art, but even a well-trained model has blind spots, and retraining the deployed model is not always safe. Single-LLM benefit is high-variance and inverts between datasets, so we pool three diverse backbones by equal-weight logit averaging, trading peak gain for a bounded worst case. On a real-world e-commerce fraud detector trained on selection-biased data, continued training regresses even when carefully tuned, whereas the overlay gains on average +2.26% recall at equal precision ($\Delta$R@P) and +1.60% precision at equal recall ($\Delta$P@R) over pro

unclustered.title: Remembering Is Not Enough: Evaluating Timing and Omission in Longitudinal AI Mental Health Support
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluations of large language models (LLMs) for mental health support commonly focus on the clinical appropriateness of individual responses, potentially overlooking failures that emerge across extended interactions. As AI assistants accumulate memory of users' circumstances and prior disclosures, this raises an accountability question: Do AI chatbots provide appropriate support as users' needs evolve? We investigate by analyzing 14,256 longitudinal simulations grounded in donated chatbot histories from 22 users, examining how a memory-equipped assistant responds to suicidal ideation, self-harm, and anxiety crises across recovery trajectories and communication styles. We introduce the Context-Aware and Readiness-Evaluative (CARE) framework, developed with mental health professionals, to assess the timing and quality of advice, including omissions. unclustered.title: AtariBench: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in Atari Gameplay
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08755v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on static visual understanding benchmarks, yet their ability to act in dynamic environments remains less well understood. By decoupling fast in-game dynamics from wall-clock inference speed, AtariBench focuses on whether models can perceive rapid visual state changes, reason over spatiotemporal dynamics, and ground actions in the current observation. Our experiments reveal substantial limitations in state-of-the-art VLMs: models often fail to infer object motion and direction, exhibit brittle sequential decision-making, and over-rely on textual interaction history despite newly appended visual feedback. unclustered.title: Intent-Aware Caching for Efficient LLM Serving
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern LLM serving systems use prefix caching to accelerate multi-turn conversational workloads. They cache the key-value states of previous conversation prefixes and reuse them when subsequent requests share the same prefix, to avoid redundant prefill computation and reduce serving latency. However, achieving a high cache hit rate remains challenging because cache reuse depends on whether a conversation continues and how soon the next turn arrives. Our analysis of real workloads shows that user intent is a useful signal for this behavior, as different intents exhibit different continuation probabilities and inter-turn delays. Based on this key insight, we propose Intent-Aware Caching (IAC), an online eviction policy that classifies requests by intent, learns lightweight reuse statistics from recent serving logs and leverages these statistics to guide an oracle-inspired eviction strategy. unclustered.title: FOSCAR: Accelerating Decode Attention over 2- and 4-Bit KV Caches through Affine Folding
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-language-model decode attention streams the key-value (KV) cache for every generated token. Packing that cache into 2-bit or 4-bit quantized integers reduces memory traffic but does not automatically translate into latency saving. Existing 2-bit fused kernels reach under 31%/15% of peak HBM throughput on H100/B200. Converting each value and applying its scale and offset before feeding Tensor Cores is a major bottleneck because instruction-issue throughput is scarce on modern GPUs. Instead of applying scale and offset to each KV value, FOSCAR uses affine folding to apply them to the other operand or the output of decode-attention matrix products, depending on the quantization scheme (token-wise or channel-wise). This reduces scale-and-offset operations by up to two orders of magnitude while preserving the dequantized attention output in exact arithmetic. unclustered.title: Generative Latent Priors for Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dominant methods for interpreting large models impose strong structural assumptions. Generative Latent Priors (GLP) are a complementary approach: a diffusion model that learns the distribution of a frozen model's activations directly, imposing no assumptions. unclustered.title: CascadeRec: Deployed Adaptive LLM Compute Allocation for Multi-Tenant Content Recommendation
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08566v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are attractive rerankers for recommendation. Running an expensive model on every request is costly, and for users with sparse interaction histories it often lowers quality. We present CascadeRec, a two-tier LLM reranking cascade deployed in production at a large financial planning and analysis (FP&A) SaaS provider. It serves content recommendations to enterprise tenants on AWS EKS and GKE. A lightweight Tier-1 model reranks every request. A router escalates only the requests where extra inference-time compute is likely to help, and sends them to a more expensive Tier-2 procedure (self-consistency sampling, multi-path reasoning, or a larger model). The system has run in a production A/B experiment for over a month. unclustered.headline: CascadeRec Deploys Adaptive LLM Compute for Multi-Tenant Recommendations

unclustered.title: VoluCompose: Constructing Compact Volumetric Visual Representations for Medical Image Understanding
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08649v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medical vision--language models can interpret volumetric images, but processing full volumes is costly because hundreds of slices produce long, redundant visual-token sequences. Its hyperbolic token composition module groups contiguous slices into ordered support units and uses the Lorentz distance to account for feature magnitude and direction during token allocation, anchor selection, and refinement. unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08999v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI serving is an extremely capital-intensive endeavor that demands rapid, step-change improvements in capital efficiency to prevent industry wide increases in the cost of capital from limiting growth plans. We have explored workload isolation as a foundational, fleet-level lever for increasing capital efficiency. Isolation is the practice of intelligently grouping "like" requests before execution. unclustered.title: UniRGBA: Unifying RGB and Alpha in Pretrained Video Diffusion Models
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09069v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in video diffusion models have achieved remarkable photorealistic RGB synthesis, yet generating videos with a native alpha channel remains an open challenge. unclustered.title: Large Language Model Deployment on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices: A Practitioners Survey
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09075v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed many areas of artificial intelligence (AI), but their substantial resource requirements limit their deployment on mobile and edge devices. Although LLMs have demonstrated impressive capabilities in various applications, the next challenge is deploying these models on resource-limited edge devices. Recent innovations in software optimizations and specialized hardware have made it feasible to deploy LLMs on edge devices. Edge deployment offers benefits including local data processing, cost savings, reduced latency, and personalized responses. This paper reviews the latest techniques that make the deployment of LLMs on edge devices feasible.
unclustered.headline: Survey Maps LLM Deployment on Edge Devices

unclustered.title: The Invisible Gap: Romanized Indic Generation Fails Where Automatic Metrics Succeed
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09085v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hundreds of millions of Indians communicate with digital systems in romanized Latin characters -- typing "aap kaise hain" rather than native script -- yet romanized Indic generation is absent from NLP benchmarks and evaluation frameworks. We demonstrate that automatic metrics (BGE-M3, BERTScore) systematically misrepresent the quality of romanized Hindi, Telugu, and Kannada generation. We evaluate four LLMs (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 2.5-flash, Qwen3.5-35B) on 142 OpenAssistant query-response pairs. On a 72-response diagnostic subset, native speakers rate GPT-5.5 1.43 points higher than Claude Opus 4.8 on a 12-point rubric, whereas their full-dataset BGE-M3 means differ by only 0.004. Two distinct model-specific failure modes emerge: Gemini produces script spillage (16.9% of Telugu responses leak native script), while Qwen collapses to English-only output (16.2% of Kannada responses). unclustered.headline: AI Struggles with Romanized Indic Languages

unclustered.title: SPDMX: Large-Scale Open Stem Audio From Symbolic Music
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09140v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large public datasets have driven recent progress in machine learning, from text and vision to speech and general audio. Music remains an outlier, as copyright blocks redistribution of training audio, while many modern tasks need individual stems rather than mixtures. Existing multitrack resources trade off realism, scale, and licensing, while synthetic alternatives rely on proprietary VSTs or naive open rendering that yields weak stems. The authors intervene on the model through an intermediate swap that exchanges the activation’s J-Lens coordinates for the intermediate and a counterfactual intermediate. They show that this causally flips the model’s output toward the counterfactual answer, and argue that this flip runs through the intermediate concept because the swap takes effect earlier than a direct answer swap.We reproduce this in eight open-source models with published Neuronpedia lenses; however, we challenge whether the intermediate swap really acts through the intermediate, or through its overlap

unclustered.title: Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments for Test-Time Selection
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling test-time compute has proven highly effective at improving LLM reasoning. A popular method is best-of-n sampling, where a model generates many candidate solutions and one is selected. This motivates the question: how can we select the best candidate? When humans make choices, we find it more natural to compare two options than judge each in isolation. unclustered.title: Pdb or Not to Be: Comparing Debugging Interfaces With Pass$_{X}$@$k$
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactive debuggers are indispensable to human software development, yet coding agents overwhelmingly rely on edit-execute-observe loops, using common bash tools, test scripts, and print statements to debug via repeated shell commands. Stepping through a debugger provides live access to runtime state, which may enable different problem-solving capabilities. However, prior work typically introduces the debugger as an additional tool or through a new subagent, making its individual contribution difficult to isolate from the associated scaffold changes. To address this, we compare a debugger-only agent against a bash-only agent on all 500 SWE-bench Verified instances, holding the rest of the scaffold fixed. We evaluate both architectures on two models, GPT-OSS-120B and Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B, with three independent runs per architecture $\times$ model configuration. Crucially, to distinguish interface specialization from expanded coverage u
unclustered.headline: Study Compares Interactive Debuggers for Coding Agents

unclustered.title: ChainFlow: Few-Step Latent Flow Matching for Speculative Decoding
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speculative decoding has become a standard way to accelerate LLM inference: a lightweight drafter proposes tokens that the target verifies in one parallel pass. Existing drafters face trade-offs that limits their speedups: autoregressive drafters generate tokens one at a time, so drafting cost grows with draft length, while diffusion drafters generate tokens in parallel but predict each position independently, ignoring inter-token dependencies. We introduce ChainFlow, a new speculative decoding paradigm and the first flow-matching drafter conditioned on the target's hidden states. ChainFlow treats drafting as a short transport over hidden states, needing one or two flow steps instead of the many denoising steps of generation from noise. A variational autoencoder compresses these states so drafting cost barely grows with target size, lightweight feedback heads restore inter-token dependencies, and tree drafting raises acceptance. On Qwen3.
unclustered.headline: ChainFlow Accelerates LLM Inference via Speculative Decoding

unclustered.title: Cancellation Is Not Enough: What Retries Leave Behind in an Overloaded LLM Engine
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clients and proxies in front of an LLM engine retry calls that time out. After a transient overload, these retries can keep the engine from recovering even when calls arrive below its capacity. In this paper, we test it on vLLM with overload experiments on three open models, and with scheduler traces of one that follow each client attempt to the execution it creates in the engine. We find that with retries on, cancellation alone did not restore service in any run, and only 12-38% of the calls that arrived after the overload were delivered. The traces suggest why: retries that vLLM ran typically started prefill less than half a second before they timed out. Executions that vLLM later aborted took 79-85% of the prompt tokens it computed, and vLLM's prompt-token counter missed a third to half of all computed prompt tokens.
unclustered.headline: LLM Engine Retries Can Prevent Overload Recovery

unclustered.title: AlterNet: Adaptive-Depth Mixture-of-Experts with Learned Halting for Elastic Inference
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most LLM architectures have fixed compute demands determined at training time. We propose a novel architecture that combines the Mixture-of-Experts architecture with shallow experts and a novel dynamic-depth system to make the extent of a forward pass dynamically adjustable. Our approach lets the model automatically determine the compute needed for a given task, paired with a system to scale it down after training without retraining when the execution environment demands faster or cheaper inference. To achieve this, we introduce an iterative computation mechanism, sequence-level depth-based routing steered by a halting mechanism within the experts, a depth encoding that lets the model track its progress in the chain, and a regularization mechanism that incentivizes the model to use allocated compute efficiently. unclustered.headline: AlterNet Introduces Adaptive-Depth Mixture-of-Experts

unclustered.title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet they remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks that circumvent safety mechanisms and elicit harmful or unintended outputs. Such sequential optimization may be suboptimal because the optimal intervention location can depend on the intervention applied there, and vice versa. unclustered.headline: AttentionSwitch Defends LLMs Against Jailbreak Attacks

unclustered.title: Debate to Deceive: Poisoning LLM's Fact-Checking via Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Debate
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge attacks on Large Language Models, such as manipulating fact-checking judgments, pose significant risks to AI reliability. unclustered.headline: Debate Attack Manipulates LLM Fact-Checking Systems

unclustered.title: Jacobian-Causal Memory Control for Persistent Memory in Language Model Systems
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Persistent-memory systems choose not only which records are retrieved but which prior information can alter current inference. unclustered.headline: Jacobian-Causal Control for LLM Persistent Memory

unclustered.title: Aligning, Fast and Slow: A Control-Theoretic Oversight Framework for Long-Horizon Trajectories and Maintained Deployments
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents can pass checks on individual tasks while retaining memory or code changes that alter their later behavior. unclustered.title: I Think, Therefore I Attack: Evaluating Thought Injection Attacks on Reasoning Agents
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) are one of the key components of current agentic systems. unclustered.title: Notwithstanding Anything to the Contrary, Ignore All Instructions: Measuring Prompt Injection Guards on Legal Contract Review Attacks
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Specialized prompt injection guards are deployed in front of document analysis systems, but no false positive rate has been published for any of them on legal contracts. A cascaded LLM solution, where the positives of a mid-tier model are verified by a frontier model, is 6.5x cheaper than using exclusively a frontier model and approaches its performance.
unclustered.headline: Prompt Injection Guards Tested on Legal Contract Review

unclustered.title: When F1 Is Not Enough: Auditing Codebooks for LLM-Assisted Annotation
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for text annotation in social science, but standard performance metrics do not explain why errors occur. unclustered.title: Learning Whom to Trust About the Unseen: Source Credibility and Reliability Transfer in Language Models
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A source who has been right before deserves attention, but about what? unclustered.title: Rethinking Agent Trajectory Compression: A Workflow-Aware Perspective
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As long-horizon agents increasingly rely on multi-step tool interactions to accomplish complex tasks, their execution trajectories continuously accumulate structured outputs and intermediate artifacts, leading to growing context overhead. unclustered.title: Toward LLM Self-Play Under Data Scarcity: Effectiveness, Generalizability, and Trustworthiness
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid development of large language models (LLMs) has been driven largely by scaling model size and human-curated training data, yet this paradigm is increasingly constrained by data scarcity and diminishing returns from human supervision. unclustered.title: Frame: Form-Restricted Authoring with Model-Based Evaluation
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many professional reports reuse the structure of prior editions while updating the content. unclustered.title: Flex-RSI: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement of Frontier Agents
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.08946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier language models are increasingly deployed as agents, and how well an agent performs depends not only on its model but also on its harness: the prompts, tools, memory, and control loop through which the model acts. unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Behavioral evaluation of language models fixes its dimensions in advance: hallucination, sycophancy, toxicity, over-refusal. unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reasoning traces improve vision-language models on complex multimodal tasks, but forcing every input to follow a long reasoning process leads to overthinking and unnecessary inference cost. unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although time-series foundation models (TSFMs) achieve strong zero-shot transferability across high-information-density physical systems, applying overparameterized TSFMs to quantitative finance is fundamentally constrained by low signal-to-noise ratios, non-stationarity, and prohibitive autoregressive decoding latency. unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) play an increasing role in programming education, challenging traditional assessment methods as they can generate fully functional code instantly. unclustered.title: Nudging Decision Models: Do Digital Nudges Steer Fast, Generation-Free AI Agents?
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based agents increasingly automate business and consumer tasks but are slow and expensive. unclustered.title: An Empirical Study of Issues in GPU Kernel Libraries for LLM Systems

unclustered.title: Challenges, Opportunities, and Misconceptions in Neurosymbolic AI
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine opportunities for neurosymbolic AI alongside increasingly powerful neural models, particularly with regards to efficiency, safety and interpretability. unclustered.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weight-Space Programming (WSP) enables reasoning agents to directly inspect and modify neural network parameters, offering an alternative to gradient-based model adaptation. unclustered.title: Against All Likelihood
unclustered.summary: arXiv:2611.09385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maximum likelihood is the dominant training principle for large language models, yet likelihood is neither necessary nor sufficient for truth.
